I'd like to work on this. To narrow it down, could you share your environment (iOS/Android, Safari/Chrome/installed PWA), a screenshot of the oversized spacing, and whether it happens with the keyboard open or closed?

From reading the code, safe-area handling is centralized in `layout-new.tsx`, which applies both `env(safe-area-inset-top)` and `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` as root padding whenever `viewport-fit=cover` is active. Two scenarios could make this look oversized:

1. In regular mobile Safari/Chrome (not installed PWA), `dvh` already accounts for the browser chrome, so adding the insets again can double the spacing.
2. With `interactive-widget=resizes-content`, when the keyboard opens, the layout shrinks but `safe-area-inset-bottom` can still report the home-indicator inset (~34px), leaving a phantom gap above the keyboard.

Happy to scope the fix once we know which case you're hitting — likely either gating the padding to standalone/PWA mode or using `max(0px, calc(...))` logic.

Seeing what looks like the same startup race with a headless `opencode serve` (1.18.18, Linux), driven by an SDK client (Paseo daemon), so this is not desktop-specific.

Timeline from the client journal plus opencode.db timestamps: the server answers HTTP (session.create) 2 seconds after spawn, but a /global/event subscription opened right at startup delivers nothing, not even the initial greeting, for 30+ seconds. The client's 30s first-record deadline fires and the run dies. The consumer recovers on a later reconnect against the same server and session.

Once a server is past startup, fresh subscribers get their first SSE record in a few ms (checked against 18 running servers), so the bad window is only right around boot. Happy to share logs and timestamps if useful.

Confirmed still broken on **1.18.22** (current latest) and reconfirmed on **1.18.21** — same signature, same "Failed to reload [project]" toast / empty model list / full crash depending on where it lands. Still unable to reliably open the app since v1.18.4.

Did a fuller elimination pass this time, ruling out several suspected causes one at a time (several launches per condition):

- **Custom `npm` providers**: still crashes with **zero** `npm`-based providers configured (only a built-in catalog provider active) — not caused by custom providers specifically.
- **Cache/local state**: still crashes after fully wiping Chromium cache, Local/Session Storage, and the models.dev catalog cache.
- **Default model resolution**: still crashes even with a genuinely-connected, currently-selected built-in model (`opencode/x-preview-f-free`, an OpenCode Zen free model) pinned as the top-level `model` config — so it's not simply "no default model resolves."
- Roughly 40-60% of launches/reloads hit it in our testing; the rest are clean. Reads as a real timing race, not a deterministic config issue.

Possible code-level lead, for whoever picks this up: `packages/app/src/context/global-sync/utils.ts`'s `normalizeAgentList` (~line 23) reads `agent.request.settings.temperature` unguarded. The early-return guard on line 16 only covers the case where *every* agent lacks `request` entirely — it doesn't cover a partial/mixed list where one agent has `request` but no `request.settings`. Separately, `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts`'s `defaultModel()`/`getModel()` depend on the target provider already being present in the live in-memory registry (`s.providers`), which is populated asynchronously — a plausible source of a transiently-undefined `settings` for a given agent, though we couldn't confirm this is the exact mechanism.
Closing to restart with a narrower Gemini-only scope.

The MCP server approach suggested by @samvallad33 and @robertn702 is definitely the cleanest interface boundary for OpenCode—it decouples storage from the core binary without requiring heavy database dependencies.

The architectural challenge with simply indexing raw session transcripts or loading flat markdown files is **state invalidation**. When a project migrates (e.g. upgrading from Next.js 14 to 15 or changing an API endpoint), a flat memory file or raw transcript retains both the old pattern and the new pattern. The model inevitably retrieves conflicting facts and hallucinates.

The standard pattern to solve this is an append-only SVO (Subject-Verb-Object) event ledger with explicit `valid_to` chronological bounds. When a new decision is stored (`[Auth] -> [Uses] -> [JWT]`), it closes the `valid_to` timestamp of the prior conflicting fact (`[Auth] -> [Uses] -> [SessionCookies]`). Retrieval queries simply filter `WHERE valid_to IS NULL`.

Whether implemented via local SQLite or a managed backend, adding temporal supersession to the MCP tool definition ensures old project history never pollutes fresh sessions.

Building off what was already posted here, I got SHIFT+ENTER to work by doing this:

Open Windows Terminal. Press Ctrl+Shift+, (comma) to open your raw settings.json file.

Add this code block inside your top-level "actions"
```
{
  "command": { "action": "sendInput", "input": "\u001b[13;2u" },
  "id": "User.sendInput.ShiftEnterCustom"
}
```

Add this code block inside your top-level "keybindings"
```
{
  "keys": "shift+enter",
  "id": "User.sendInput.ShiftEnterCustom"
}
```

Re the related-PR scan above (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/44242#issuecomment-5382596858) — I went through all three, no duplication:

- **#11377** is a different meaning of "tier": a cost class on the task tool that picks *which model* a subagent runs on (`quick`/`standard`/`advanced`). This PR's `tier` classifies a *given* model's capability (`minimal`/`default`) to size its prompt, tool roster, and schemas. Orthogonal features; only textual overlap (both add a task-tool parameter), so whichever lands second rebases `task.ts`. The naming collision might be worth resolving if both are accepted.
- **#39397** is complementary: it recovers when a model burns its whole output cap on reasoning (`finish === "length"` → keep looping). This PR reduces how often that happens (window-derived output cap instead of the 32k assumption), and its turn budgets would bound that auto-continue loop for models that truncate every step. They compose well.
- **#43713** is the closest neighbor and also composes: it makes compaction fields per-model overridable; this PR changes what the *default* is when nobody sets one (proportional reserve instead of flat 20k, honest zero-limit handling). Natural resolution order: model override → global config → proportional default. Both touch `overflow.ts`/`compaction.ts`, so the second to land has a mechanical rebase.

Happy to rebase over any of them if they merge first.

Related opencode issues discovered in a tracker/web sweep:

- **#43731 (open, `2.0`)** — the closest relation: `session.hook("context")` mutations of *existing message parts* are persisted back into session storage (by part id). Its author notes opencode's own plan-mode plugin "splices a synthetic user message into `t.messages`" — i.e. the documented/intended contract is that the mutated array **is** the dispatch payload. Worth noting: our probe only ever **appended new messages / new parts**; we never tried mutating an *existing* part's text in place (which is what #43731 says has real server-side effect). That distinction may be the key to a working injection path and is worth a targeted follow-up test.
- **#39674 (closed)** — same bug class in a different hook: `tool.execute.before` mutations to `output.args` do not propagate to tool execution. Evidence that "hook mutation not propagating" is a known, being-fixed class of V2 bug, not unique to the context hook.
- **#35966 (closed, `2.0`)** — design decision on how synthetic prompts enter the Session inbox; defines the intended synthetic-message semantics we found filtered out of the model prompt.
- **#27899 (closed)** — feature request for a headless prompt-mutation hook (a `tui.prompt.append` analog for `opencode run`); the same capability gap (injecting context before dispatch) from the headless side.
- **#35728 (open)** — `background.extend()` cannot inject messages into active session loops; another manifestation of injection-into-session being unavailable.
- **#14808 (closed, V1-era)** — "session.created not firing" on 1.2.10; same symptom family under the old plugin model, closed since.

So the pattern across V2 is: **event delivery to plugin subscribers and hook-mutation propagation to the dispatched request are both unreliable as of beta-18050**, while the public SSE endpoint and the session store behave differently from the plugin channel (and from each other).

Responses to the review findings — all addressed in the latest push except where server support is required (this PR is intentionally app-only):

**[P1] Defer model/agent changes until queue delivery** — Fixed. `sendPrompt` now applies `switchAgent`/`switchModel` only for steer deliveries; a queued follow-up no longer reconfigures the turn it waits behind and runs with the session selection at delivery time. Caveat: honoring a *different* selection per queued prompt at delivery time needs per-prompt selection in the admission API (server change, out of scope here); the intended selection stays recorded in the prompt metadata.

**[P1] Make queue rewrites atomic** — Mitigated client-side. Clones are now admitted under client-minted IDs, and when an original's cancellation conflicts (it delivered because the turn hit its idle boundary mid-rebuild), its clone is withdrawn instead — so the race degrades to "reorder didn't apply", never duplicate execution or loss. True atomicity needs a server-side reorder endpoint.

**[P1] Do not cancel before admitting an edited steer** — Fixed. The steer is admitted first; the original is cancelled only once the steer exists. A failed admission leaves the original queued and restores the edited text into the composer for retry.

**[P2] Wait for optimistic admission before rebuilding an edit** — Fixed. `rebuildQueue` merges locally known queued rows whose admission echo has not landed into the authoritative list; clone admissions chain behind the in-flight POST per session, so the subsequent cancel targets an admitted row.

**[P2] Restore the complete draft state after editing** — Fixed. The stash now captures mode and the retry marker; `cancelEdit` restores mode, prompt, then retry (both mode and prompt writes clear retry, hence the order).

**[P2] Preserve review-comment instructions during edits** — Fixed. `payload.text` is display text plus appended comment notes; an edit now replaces only the display part and re-appends the notes, so the model-visible instructions survive.

**[P2] Disable reordering while editing** — Fixed. Sortables are disabled while an edit is open (and while a rebuild is in flight), and `reorder` guards re-entry, so a re-minted ID can never orphan the edit stash.

**[P2] Order revert cancellation against admissions** — Improved within app-only constraints: revert now cancels the union of the authoritative inbox list and the local snapshot (still fire-and-forget so restore is not delayed). An admission still in flight when the list is fetched can survive the sweep; fully closing that requires a server-side revert-discards-inbox rule — flagged in the code comment as follow-up.

New coverage: "steering an edited prompt admits the steer before cancelling the original" asserts the admission/cancel ordering; the queue suite is now 8 e2e tests, full app suite still green.
